concepts.title: Force - A Push or Pull
concepts.definition: An external influence as a push or pull that can change an object's state of motion, speed, direction, or shape.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: A force is fundamentally a push or a pull acting on an object.

concepts.title: Forces due to Interaction
concepts.definition: The mutual action between at least two bodies that gives a force acting on each of them.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: A force cannot exist in isolation; it requires interaction between two or more objects.

solution_steps.explain: Determine the two objects that are interacting to produce the force.
Confirm that both bodies exert a force on each other, since a force cannot arise from a single body alone.
State that without interaction between at least two bodies, no force can come into play.

concepts.title: Net Force in Same Direction
concepts.definition: The total force acting on an object when multiple forces are applied along the exact same line of action and direction, calculated by summing their magnitudes.
concepts.key_idea: Forces acting in the common direction combine by addition.

concepts.title: Net Force in Opposite Directions
concepts.definition: The resultant force acting on an object when two forces are applied in directly opposing directions, calculated as the absolute difference between their magnitudes.
concepts.key_idea: Forces acting in opposite directions oppose each other and subtract.

concepts.title: Muscular Force
concepts.definition: The contact force applied by the action of muscles inside a living body.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Internal muscles exert forces to perform physical tasks like lifting, pushing, or breathing.
question_patterns: what is muscular force

solution_steps.explain: Verify if the force originates from the contraction or expansion of muscles in a living organism.
Confirm that the muscle applies the force through direct contact with the object, making muscular force a contact force.
Conclude that the force is muscular force since it is produced by muscles and requires physical contact.

concepts.title: Force of Friction
concepts.definition: A resistive contact force that acts between surfaces touching to oppose their relative motion.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Friction always pushes against the way surfaces slide, slowing moving things down.
question_patterns: what is friction
why does a rolling ball stop
in which direction does friction act
how does force of friction work
list the main features of force of friction

solution_steps.action: Identify relative motion and surface contact
solution_steps.explain: Friction arises when two surfaces slide or attempt to slide past each other.
Friction always acts opposite to the direction of relative motion or intended motion between the surfaces.

solution_steps.action: Conclude that friction is a contact force
solution_steps.explain: State that friction is a resistive contact force that opposes motion and eventually brings moving objects to rest.

concepts.title: Electrostatic Force
concepts.definition: A push or pull from a distance: one charged body acting on another body, charged or not.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Charges can attract or repel each other from a distance without physical contact.
question_patterns: what is electrostatic force
explain why a rubbed straw attracts another straw
is electrostatic force a contact force
short note on electrostatic force

solution_steps.explain: Verify if the force is caused by electric charges acquired through friction or other means.

solution_steps.action: Check for attraction or repulsion at a distance
solution_steps.explain: Confirm that the charged body exerts a pull or push on another body without physical contact.

solution_steps.action: Classify the force as electrostatic and non-contact
solution_steps.explain: Conclude that the force is electrostatic since it arises from charges and acts from a distance without direct contact.

concepts.title: Gravitational Force
concepts.definition: The attractive non-contact force that pulls objects toward each other, most noticeably pulling objects toward the Earth's center.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Every object in the universe exerts an attractive pull on every other object.
question_patterns: what is gravity
why do leaves fall to the ground
is gravitational force attractive or repulsive
describe gravitational force with an example
what do you understand by gravitational force

solution_steps.explain: Gravity is the universal attractive force acting between any two masses.
Confirm that the objects are pulled toward each other without any physical contact between them.

solution_steps.action: Classify the force as gravitational and non-contact
solution_steps.explain: Conclude that the force is gravitational since it is an attractive non-contact force acting between masses.

concepts.title: Pressure
concepts.definition: The amount of perpendicular force distributed over a unit surface area.
concepts.key_idea: Pressure varies in inverse proportion with the area over which a force is indeed applied.

concepts.title: Pressure Exerted by Liquids
concepts.definition: A fluid presses on the bottom and the walls of its container, and this pressure grows with the depth of the liquid column.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Liquids exert pressure in all directions, and this pressure is equal at the same depth.
question_patterns: does liquid exert pressure on walls

why does a rubber sheet bulge when water is poured

solution_steps.explain: Liquid pressure depends on depth and acts perpendicular to the container walls.

solution_steps.explain: Confirm that the liquid exerts pressure on the bottom as well as the side walls of the container.

concepts.title: Atmospheric Pressure
concepts.definition: The pressure exerted by the weight of the air column in the atmosphere acting on a unit area.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: The massive weight of air above us exerts a huge pressure, which is balanced by our internal body pressure.
question_patterns: what is atmospheric pressure
why are we not crushed by atmospheric pressure
how does a rubber sucker stick to a wall
explain atmospheric pressure in your own words
describe atmospheric pressure with an example

solution_steps.explain: Atmospheric pressure is caused by the gravitational pull on the air column extending above the surface.

solution_steps.action: Verify the pressure acts on all surfaces
solution_steps.explain: Confirm that the weight of air presses equally on all exposed surfaces, including objects and our bodies.

solution_steps.action: Explain why we are not crushed
solution_steps.explain: Conclude that our internal body pressure balances the atmospheric pressure, preventing us from being crushed.
